newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia gives Bre-X, Barrick new Busang deadline.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia gives Bre-X, Barrick new Busang deadline.

text.p: Indonesian Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana said on Friday that Canada's Bre-X Minerals Ltd and Barrick Gold Corp had reversed an earlier agreement on the huge Busang gold find.
"Until December 12 afternoon they had said they had agreed. But last night, there was a 180 degree change," he told reporters after meeting Indonesia's President Suharto.
"I don't know the situation. Who influenced, we don't know. They don't agree with what has been agreed to with the government," he said.
"I will wait for them," he added. "This is also the advice of the president...give them a chance until end of December. I forget the date, but there is a limit."
The Indonesian government has been pushing Bre-X to form a partnership with Barrick in developing the Busang property, estimated by Bre-X to contain at least 57 million ounces of gold.

The government wants Bre-X, which discovered the gold, to retain a 25-percent stake, with Barrick taking 75 percent. Out of the total, it wants the two companies to allocate 10 percent to the government.

The ministry's secretary-general, Umar Said, said on Thursday that Bre-X and Barrick had agreed to the proposal and they had to set up a joint venture and make a fresh application for contracts of work if they wanted to develop the find.
Bre-X Chief Executive David Walsh told Reuters in Toronto on Thursday that talks between the Alberta-based company and Barrick were moving ahead, but at a snail's pace.

Walsh also said he still had high hopes that Suharto would allow an auction of Bre-X's stake in Busang, adding that although the company had not solicited offers, it had been getting offers from other companies.
He said he had spoken to executives at Vancouver-based Placer Dome Inc, Newmont Mining Corp and Teck Corp.
Sudjana said on Friday that if Bre-X and Barrick failed to reach an agreement, local laws would become effective.
"President Suharto has advised that if they don't match, it's all right. Our laws will become effective," he said without elaborating.
"But we will give them a chance...to continue with their negotiations. This is the wisdom of the president," he said.
Sudjana also said the parliamentary approval in July of an application for contracts of work by Bre-X to develop the richest parts of the find, Busang II and III, was still valid.
Asked if the parliamentary approval for the application by Bre-X had been cancelled, Sudjana said, "Not yet."
"When they form a new (joint-venture) company, they need to submit a new application," he said.
"It will be automatically cancelled," he said when asked what will happen to the existing application by Bre-X.

On Wednesday, Sudjana said after appearing before a marathon parliamentary commission that the parliamentary approval had been cancelled. "We cancelled it. The Bre-X contract of work will be processed from the beginning," he told reporters.
The minister on Friday did not explain the reversal of his earlier statement.
